# InjectContracts two-phase deploy: baseline then block-0 hardfork overlay

**Status:** verified · **Subsystem:** A8 (Genesis & Bootstrap) · **Type:** B3

InjectContracts seeds genesis.Alloc with system contract code and
storage in two ordered phases. Phase 1 calls
GetSystemContractsTransition with config.Anzeon.SystemContracts —
this deploys every v1 contract and runs each initializeXxx() to
populate its full Solidity storage layout. Phase 2 iterates
config.CollectUpgrades() and applies, for each upgrade whose block
is 0, applyUpgradeOverlay onto the same Alloc. The overlay path
REPLACES the contract Code only and merges any explicit State
entries; pre-existing Balance and Storage from Phase 1 are
preserved. Upgrades whose Block is not 0 are skipped at genesis
time and are instead applied at runtime by Engine.processFinalize
when the chain reaches their activation height.

# Justification + locking — why view changes preserve safety

**Status:** verified · **Subsystem:** A14 (Protocol Foundations & Design Philosophy) · **Type:** B4

In PBFT/QBFT/WBFT, a PRE-PREPARE proposed in round r > 0 MUST carry
a JUSTIFICATION proving it is consistent with what previous rounds
may have committed: a quorum of ROUND-CHANGE messages plus, if any
validator was already "locked" on a value, the PREPARE certificate
for that locked value. WBFT enforces this in preprepare.go: a new
proposal attaches `JustificationRoundChanges` and `Justification
Prepares` (preprepare.go:69, :79); the receiver validates them via
`isJustified(...)` (preprepare.go:135) before accepting the
preprepare. The locking discipline says: once you Prepare on a
value, you stay locked until a higher round shows a quorum-justified
different value — this is what guarantees that a view change cannot
silently overwrite a previously Committed block.

Implication: any change to the preprepare validator, round-change
payload format, or the message handler that handles justification
payloads (consensus/wbft/core/handler.go:265–292) directly affects
the SAFETY proof. Skipping `isJustified` for a "fast path", or
loosening which payloads count as justification, is a SAFETY
violation — two conflicting blocks can both reach quorum. This is
the single most subtle place in WBFT and the most common
hand-rolled-PBFT bug.

## Invariants
- Each handler is idempotent for duplicate messages from the same sender at the same view (sequence, round).
- Per-round state progresses strictly StatePreprepared -> StatePrepared -> StateCommitted; out-of-order messages are buffered or rejected.

# System contract storage slot layout helpers (CalculateMappingSlot / CalculateDynamicSlot / EncodeBytesToSlots)

**Status:** verified · **Subsystem:** A4 (System Contracts (Governance × 5)) · **Type:** B2

All Go-side genesis seeders for the 0x100x governance contracts follow the
EVM/Solidity storage-slot rules through a toolbox in systemcontracts/stateutil.go:
CalculateMappingSlot(baseSlot, key) = keccak256(leftPad32(key) || baseSlot) for
mapping fields; CalculateDynamicSlot(baseSlot, i) = keccak256(leftPad32(baseSlot)) + i
for the i-th element of dynamic arrays / spilled bytes chunks; IncrementHash(baseSlot, n)
= baseSlot + n to pair an EnumerableSet value slot with its companion index slot;
VarLenBytesToMultipleHash / EncodeBytesToSlots implement Solidity short/long bytes
packing (<=31B packed in the base slot, >31B spills 32B chunks); GetBytes reverses it
for reads; EnumerableSet (NewEnumerableSet / NewAddressSet) bundles the value+index
slot pair used by ValidatorList and minterList. Every storage write a Go initializer
emits is a params.StateParam with Key = a slot hash derived above and a 32-byte Value.

# GovValidator genesis initialization (initializeValidator)

**Status:** verified · **Subsystem:** A4 (System Contracts (Governance × 5)) · **Type:** B2

initializeValidator is the Go-side seeder that writes the GovValidator
(0x1001) contract storage at genesis from systemContracts.govValidator.params.
It runs initializeBase to seed inherited GovBase fields, writes the blsPoP
precompile address and the gasTip (supplied value or params.InitialGasTip),
then — when the validators/blsPublicKeys params are supplied — cross-validates
len(members) == len(validators) == len(blsPublicKeys) and walks the validator
list, emitting StateParam writes for the __validators EnumerableSet (length +
array element + index mapping), the validatorToOperator / operatorToValidator
inverse mappings, the validatorToBlsKey bytes mapping, and the
blsKeyToValidator mapping keyed by raw BLS bytes. Duplicate addresses are
skipped; the length write fires only if at least one validator was seeded.

## Pitfalls
- Changing a SLOT_VALIDATOR_* constant (or the Solidity field order) without migrating existing storage and reindexing every reader (ValidatorList, GetBLSPublicKey, GetGasTip and the EnumerableSet helpers) silently corrupts validator-set reads. # WBFT validator set construction and proposer selection

**Status:** verified · **Subsystem:** A3 (WBFT Validator Set & Epoch) · **Type:** B1

An in-memory WBFT validator set is built by the validator package:
New(addr, blsKey) wraps one validator (defaultValidator) and
NewSet(addrs, blsKeys, policy) / NewSetByValidators(validators, policy)
build a defaultSet. newDefaultSet seeds the set's validators slice in
the order the caller supplied — there is no internal sort — and picks
the proposer selector based on policy.Id: roundRobinProposer for the
RoundRobin policy (advances by seed = lastProposerIndex + round + 1)
and stickyProposer for the Sticky policy (same seed minus the +1, so
the proposer stays put across rounds with the same lastProposer).
defaultSet protects mutations of validators with validatorMu (RWMutex);
CalcProposer recomputes the active proposer via the selected selector,
and QuorumSize returns ceil(N - (N-1)/3) — the WBFT 2N/3 quorum over
equal-power validators. The deterministic order that callers feed in
is the ordering that all selectors then index into.

# Epoch transition: how the next epoch's validator set is selected and pinned

**Status:** verified · **Subsystem:** A3 (WBFT Validator Set & Epoch) · **Type:** B3

go-stablenet's validator set is fixed for the duration of an epoch
(10 blocks on Mainnet, 140 on Testnet). On the last block of each
epoch, the engine calls buildEpochInfo: it queries GovValidator
(system contract 0x1001) for the new candidate list and validator
indices, then writes an EpochInfo into that block's
Header.Extra.WBFTExtra.EpochInfo. From the next block onward,
GetValidators returns the new set; intra-epoch blocks omit
EpochInfo. Backend.GetValidatorsForVerifying provides the previous
epoch's set in parallel so cross-epoch block verification can match
signers against the correct validator set.

# GovValidator (0x1001): storage layout and validator-set governance

**Status:** needs_verification · **Subsystem:** A4 (System Contracts (Governance × 5)) · **Type:** B2

GovValidator is the system contract at address 0x1001 that owns the
on-chain validator set. Its storage layout is defined by the
SLOT_VALIDATOR_* constants in systemcontracts/gov_validator.go, which
MUST mirror the slot annotations in solidity/v1/GovValidator.sol:
blsPoP precompile address (0x32), the __validators EnumerableSet.AddressSet
(value slot 0x33 + length, index mapping at 0x34), validatorToOperator
(0x35), operatorToValidator (0x36), validatorToBlsKey (0x37),
blsKeyToValidator (0x38) and gasTip (0x39). Slots 0x0..0x31 are reserved
for the inherited GovBase. initializeValidator seeds all of these at
genesis from systemContracts.govValidator.params (members, validators,
blsPublicKeys, optional gasTip), keeping the validators array, the
operator<->validator mappings and the BLS-key mappings index-aligned per
member. Mutating the set at runtime goes through GovBase's m-of-n
governance: an active member calls configureValidator (direct, gated by
onlyActiveMember) for its own slot, while quorum changes go through
proposeChangeQuorum / proposeAddMember / proposeRemoveMember +
approveProposal, which auto-executes once approvals reach the snapshotted
quorum (requiredApprovals).

# WBFT quorum size calculation

**Status:** verified · **Subsystem:** A1 (WBFT Consensus Core) · **Type:** B3

WBFT requires QuorumSize = ceil(N - F) where N is the validator set
size and F = (N-1)/3 evaluated in float64. The quorum is the minimum
count of Prepare or Commit messages needed before the consensus core
advances state. State advancement in handlePrepareMsg uses the
expression WBFTPrepares.Size() >= valSet.QuorumSize().

ceil(N - F) is the AUTHORITATIVE quorum; any reimplementation MUST
reproduce it exactly. The dangerous refactor is not int-vs-float (see
the correctness note below) but swapping the FORMULA: the PBFT-textbook
2f+1 or a simple majority N/2+1 DIVERGE from ceil(N - F) for N not of
the form 3f+1, and a lower quorum finalizes with too few honest nodes
(a safety violation). Examples: N=5 -> ceil=4 but 2f+1=3; N=6 -> ceil=5
but 2f+1=3; N=8 -> ceil=6 but 2f+1=5.

**Status:** verified · **Subsystem:** A1 (WBFT Consensus Core) · **Type:** B1

# WBFT validator set construction and proposer selection

**Status:** verified · **Subsystem:** A3 (WBFT Validator Set & Epoch) · **Type:** B1

An in-memory WBFT validator set is built by the validator package:
New(addr, blsKey) wraps one validator (defaultValidator) and
NewSet(addrs, blsKeys, policy) / NewSetByValidators(validators, policy)
build a defaultSet. newDefaultSet seeds the set's validators slice in
the order the caller supplied — there is no internal sort — and picks
the proposer selector based on policy.Id: roundRobinProposer for the

and stickyProposer for the Sticky policy (same seed minus the +1, so
the proposer stays put across rounds with the same lastProposer).

and QuorumSize returns ceil(N - (N-1)/3) — the WBFT 2N/3 quorum over
equal-power validators. The deterministic order that callers feed in

# WBFT consensus flow — actors and message sequence per height

**Status:** verified · **Subsystem:** A1 (WBFT Consensus Core) · **Type:** B1

The WBFT consensus engine drives one block per height through four
phases inside Core: handleRequest emits a Preprepare from the
current proposer; every validator broadcasts a Prepare in response;
once each validator has seen a Prepare quorum it broadcasts a Commit;
once each validator has seen a Commit quorum the block is finalised
and Core advances to the next height via startNewRound. RoundChange
fires on RequestTimeout and selects a new proposer for the same
height. Backend (consensus/wbft/backend) is the bridge between Core
and the blockchain — it broadcasts/gossips messages, signs with BLS,
fetches Validators, and commits sealed blocks back. Engine
(consensus/wbft/engine) handles header validation, BaseFee
distribution, and epoch construction. The Istanbul/100 P2P
subprotocol (A9) carries the messages between nodes.

# WBFT quorum size calculation

**Status:** verified · **Subsystem:** A1 (WBFT Consensus Core) · **Type:** B3

WBFT requires QuorumSize = ceil(N - F) where N is the validator set
size and F = (N-1)/3 evaluated in float64. The quorum is the minimum
count of Prepare or Commit messages needed before the consensus core
advances state. State advancement in handlePrepareMsg uses the
